_comment: VRAM floors enforced by tools/gpu_gate.py at dispatch time, not left to whichever engine remembers to read them. Every number here is a measurement on THIS machine (RTX 3060, 12288 MiB total), with its source named in `measured`. A rule whose need_mib is not an integer is NOT skipped and NOT guessed: it stays in force with an unreadable threshold and the gate answers UNKNOWN - it refuses. If this file is missing or malformed the gate falls back to in-code rules (3D and image diffusion both covered) and marks the decision `degraded`. Thresholds are re-read on every call on purpose: a number memorised at boot is the wrong number by next week.

rules.label: 3d-trellis
rules.measured: 2026-10-15 F7: a TRELLIS.2 image-to-3d run needed 9.73 GiB while the machine had 6.38 GiB free; weights alone stage 5004 MB (brain/skills/comfyui/05). Refusing below this floor is what prevents the OOM that surfaces as connection-loss rather than as a node error.

rules.label: image-diffusion
rules.measured: Z-Image-Turbo int8 = 5.78 GiB; the fp8 Juggernaut-Z row is 5.73 GiB (brain/skills/comfyui/08). bf16 12 GB variants do not fit beside a text encoder and are deliberately given no floor here - they are not runnable on this card at any free figure.
rules.why_removed: 'checkpoint' matched git and database checkpoint items as often as model checkpoints, so a busy GPU would have refused non-GPU work on a word collision. Matching is word-bounded now, so 'flux' no longer hits 'reflux', 'flux_store' or 'test_flux'; '.' stays a boundary because the real product name in this queue is TRELLIS.2.

rules.label: vendor-cloud
rules.measured: Runs on vendor infrastructure; zero local VRAM. Recorded as a rule with 0 so the gate is explicit about it instead of silent: the cost gate for these lives in tools/tripo.py cost_is_known(), not here.
